main_body: Four-storey school building: a green rooftop garden with parapet seen from above, over a cream facade with window bands and a ground-floor entrance
top_band: Rooftop: a light lavender parapet cap at rows 1-5, then a green roof surface at rows 7-38 (about 32 rows), closed by a bright parapet front edge at rows 39-40
evidence: The column scan at x=32, 64 and 95 meets a dark outline, then a light parapet, then a large green horizontal surface with rooftop units on it. A bright 1-2 row parapet front edge at rows 39-40 follows, then a clearly different cream facade with window bands. The top is tall for a foreshortened surface, but it reads as a real horizontal roof seen from above and is clearly separated from the vertical face. The windows have frames and sills with some inset, and the entrance has a canopy. No receding side face. Passes as 3/4, though the facade itself is fairly flat.

style.evidence: The outlines are tinted (0% neutral dark edge pixels), which is good. But the candidate has only 43 distinct colours against 66 and 185 for the references, and a 12% flat-fill share against 0% for both. The cream wall and window glass are large near-flat areas with only sparse speckle. The green roof has about 3-4 greens. Windows repeat the same pattern with little variation. Median colours per tile is 10, close to the stone house reference at 11 but well below the timber house at 18. Overall it is thinner and flatter than the Beodeul references, so I fail it under the strict standard.
